descriptionChirho: The primary adjectival sense of being at ease, tranquil, undisturbed -- describing a state of security and calm. All inflections (ms, fs, mpc) and conjunctive forms merge here. Eng 'at ease,' 'and at ease,' 'and always at ease,' 'and secure'; spa 'tranquila,' 'Tranquilo,' 'y en paz,' 'y tranquilos,' 'y en paz'; arb 'مُطْمَئِنَّةٍ,' 'مُطْمَئِنًّا,' 'وَآمِنَةً,' 'وَمُطْمَئِنّو,' 'وَهَادِئٌ'; kor '평온한,' '평안한,' '평안하게,' '평안한 자들이,' '평안하니'; swa 'tulivu,' 'nilikuwa na amani,' 'na amani,' 'na wenye-amani,' 'na utulivu'. All describe the same quality of being at peace/ease across gender and number variations.

The substantival or nominalized use of the adjective, functioning as a noun meaning 'quietness' or 'peace/peacefulness.' Eng 'quietness,' 'and peaceful'; spa 'tranquilidad,' 'y pacífica'; arb 'سَلَامًا,' 'وَآمِنَةٌ'; kor '평안을,' '그와 평화로운'; swa 'utulivu,' 'na amani'. The Arabic 'سَلَامًا' (salaam) and the nominalized English 'quietness' suggest a substantival use distinct from the purely predicative adjective, while S140741 with 'peaceful' leans toward a settled-state quality.
